title: सप्तदशोऽध्यायः

summary.en: The Samshaptakas form a half-moon array and Arjuna accepts their challenge, asking Krishna to drive to them. He blows Devadatta and slaughters their host with arrows.
summary.kn: ಸಂಶಪ್ತಕರು ಅರ್ಧಚಂದ್ರ ವ್ಯೂಹ ರಚಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಅರ್ಜುನ ಸವಾಲನ್ನು ಸ್ವೀಕರಿಸಿ ಕೃಷ್ಣನಿಗೆ ರಥ ನಡೆಸಲು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ದೇವದತ್ತ ಶಂಖ ಊದಿ ಬಾಣಗಳಿಂದ ಅವರ ಪಡೆಯನ್ನು ಸಂಹರಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: संशप्तक अर्धचन्द्र व्यूह बनाते हैं और अर्जुन चुनौती स्वीकार कर कृष्ण से रथ ले चलने को कहते हैं। वे देवदत्त शंख बजाते हैं और बाणों से उनकी सेना का संहार करते हैं।
summary.te: సంశప్తకులు అర్ధచంద్ర వ్యూహం పన్నుతారు; అర్జునుడు సవాలు స్వీకరించి రథాన్ని నడపమని కృష్ణునికి చెబుతాడు. దేవదత్త శంఖం ఊది బాణాలతో వారి సేనను హతమారుస్తాడు.
summary.ta: சம்சப்தகர் பிறை வியூகம் அமைக்க, அர்ஜுனன் சவாலை ஏற்றுத் தேரைச் செலுத்தும்படி கண்ணனுக்குக் கூறுகிறான். தேவதத்தம் முழங்கி அம்புகளால் அவர்கள் படையை அழிக்கிறான்.
summary.ml: സംശപ്തകർ അർധചന്ദ്രാകൃതിയിൽ വ്യൂഹം ചമയ്ക്കുന്നു; അവരുടെ വെല്ലുവിളി സ്വീകരിച്ച അർജുനൻ അവരുടെ അടുത്തേക്ക് തേര് ഓടിക്കാൻ കൃഷ്ണനോട് പറയുന്നു. അദ്ദേഹം ദേവദത്തം മുഴക്കി അമ്പുകൊണ്ട് അവരുടെ സേനയെ കൂട്ടക്കൊല ചെയ്യുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 7.17; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Tue Sep 22 2026

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
ततः संशप्तका राजन्समे देशे व्यवस्थिताः ।
व्यूह्यानीकं रथैरेव चन्द्रार्धाख्यं मुदान्विताः ॥

meaning.en: Then the Samshaptakas, O king, took their stand on level ground and, joyful, drew up their force of chariots in the array called the half-moon.

verses.text:
ते किरीटिनमायान्तं दृष्ट्वा हर्षेण मारिष ।
उदक्रोशन्नरव्याघ्राः शब्देन महता तदा ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the diademed Arjuna approach, those tigers among men, in their delight, raised a great shout, respected sir.

verses.text:
स शब्दः प्रदिशः सर्वा दिशः खं च समावृणोत् ।
आवृतत्वाच्च लोकस्य नासीत्तत्र प्रतिस्वनः ॥

meaning.en: That sound filled all the directions, intermediate directions and sky, and because the world was filled, there was no echo.

verses.text:
अतीव संप्रहृष्टांस्तानुपलभ्य धनंजयः ।
किंचिदभ्युत्स्मयन्कृष्णमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing them overjoyed, Dhananjaya, smiling a little, said this to Krishna.

verses.text:
पश्यैतान्देवकीमातर्मुमूर्षूनद्य संयुगे ।
भ्रातॄंस्त्रैगर्तकानेवं रोदितव्ये प्रहर्षितान् ॥

meaning.en: "Look, son of Devaki's mother, at these Trigarta brothers, about to die in battle today, exulting where they should weep.

verses.text:
अथ वा हर्षकालोऽयं त्रैगर्तानामसंशयम् ।
कुनरैर्दुरवापान्हि लोकान्प्राप्स्यन्त्यनुत्तमान् ॥

meaning.en: Or perhaps this is truly a time for the Trigartas to rejoice, for they will gain the supreme worlds that evil men can hardly reach."

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाबाहुर्हृषीकेशं ततोऽर्जुनः ।
आससाद रणे व्यूढां त्रैगर्तानामनीकिनीम् ॥

meaning.en: Having said this to Hrishikesha, the mighty-armed Arjuna approached the arrayed army of the Trigartas in battle.

verses.text:
स देवदत्तमादाय शङ्खं हेमपरिष्कृतम् ।
दध्मौ वेगेन महता फल्गुनः पूरयन्दिशः ॥

meaning.en: Taking his conch Devadatta, adorned with gold, Phalguna blew it with great force, filling the directions.

verses.text:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ता संशप्तकवरूथिनी ।
निश्चेष्टावस्थिता संख्ये अश्मसारमयी यथा ॥

meaning.en: Terrified by that sound, the Samshaptaka army stood motionless in the battle as if made of stone.

verses.text:
वाहास्तेषां विवृत्ताक्षाः स्तब्धकर्णशिरोधराः ।
विष्टब्धचरणा मूत्रं रुधिरं च प्रसुस्रुवुः ॥

meaning.en: Their draft animals, with eyes rolling, ears and necks stiff and legs rigid, let urine and blood flow.

verses.text:
उपलभ्य च ते संज्ञामवस्थाप्य च वाहिनीम् ।
युगपत्पाण्डुपुत्राय चिक्षिपुः कङ्कपत्रिणः ॥

meaning.en: Regaining their senses and steadying the force, they all together shot heron-feathered arrows at the son of Pandu.

verses.text:
तान्यर्जुनः सहस्राणि दश पञ्चैव चाशुगैः ।
अनागतान्येव शरैश्चिच्छेदाशुपराक्रमः ॥

meaning.en: Swift in valor, Arjuna cut those arrows, ten thousand and five thousand of them, with swift arrows before they reached him.

verses.text:
ततोऽर्जुनं शितैर्बाणैर्दशभिर्दशभिः पुनः ।
प्रत्यविध्यंस्ततः पार्थस्तानविध्यत्त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Then they pierced Arjuna again with sharp arrows, ten each, and Partha pierced them with three each.

verses.text:
एकैकस्तु ततः पार्थं राजन्विव्याध पञ्चभिः ।
स च तान्प्रतिविव्याध द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यां पराक्रमी ॥

meaning.en: Then each of them, O king, pierced Partha with five, and the valiant one pierced each in return with two.

verses.text:
भूय एव तु संरब्धास्तेऽर्जुनं सहकेशवम् ।
आपूरयञ्शरैस्तीक्ष्णैस्तटाकमिव वृष्टिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Again, enraged, they filled Arjuna and Keshava with sharp arrows, like rains filling a lake.

verses.text:
ततः शरसहस्राणि प्रापतन्नर्जुनं प्रति ।
भ्रमराणामिव व्राताः फुल्लद्रुमगणे वने ॥

meaning.en: Then thousands of arrows fell on Arjuna, like swarms of bees on a grove of flowering trees in the forest.

verses.text:
ततः सुबाहुस्त्रिंशद्भिरद्रिसारमयैर्दृढैः ।
अविध्यदिषुभिर्गाढं किरीटे सव्यसाचिनम् ॥

meaning.en: Then Subahu pierced the left-handed archer deeply in the crown with thirty strong arrows made of mountain iron.

verses.text:
तैः किरीटी किरीटस्थैर्हेमपुङ्खैरजिह्मगैः ।
शातकुम्भमयापीडो बभौ यूप इवोच्छ्रितः ॥

meaning.en: With those straight gold-feathered arrows stuck in his crown, the diademed Arjuna shone like a raised sacrificial post with a golden crest.

verses.text:
हस्तावापं सुबाहोस्तु भल्लेन युधि पाण्डवः ।
चिच्छेद तं चैव पुनः शरवर्षैरवाकिरत् ॥

meaning.en: The Pandava cut Subahu's hand-guard with a bhalla in the battle and covered him again with showers of arrows.

verses.text:
ततः सुशर्मा दशभिः सुरथश्च किरीटिनम् ।
सुधर्मा सुधनुश्चैव सुबाहुश्च समर्पयन् ॥

meaning.en: Then Sushrman with ten, and Surartha, Sudharma, Sudhanus and Subahu attacked the diademed Arjuna.

verses.text:
तांस्तु सर्वान्पृथग्बाणैर्वानरप्रवरध्वजः ।
प्रत्यविध्यद्ध्वजांश्चैषां भल्लैश्चिच्छेद काञ्चनान् ॥

meaning.en: The monkey-bannered one pierced each of them separately with arrows and cut their golden banners with bhallas.

verses.text:
सुधन्वनो धनुश्छित्त्वा हयान्वै न्यवधीच्छरैः ।
अथास्य सशिरस्त्राणं शिरः कायादपाहरत् ॥

meaning.en: He cut Sudhanvan's bow and killed his horses with arrows, and then took his head with its helmet from his body.

verses.text:
तस्मिंस्तु पतिते वीरे त्रस्तास्तस्य पदानुगाः ।
व्यद्रवन्त भयाद्भीता येन दौर्योधनं बलम् ॥

meaning.en: When that hero fell, his followers, terrified, ran in fear toward Duryodhana's army.

verses.text:
ततो जघान संक्रुद्धो वासविस्तां महाचमूम् ।
शरजालैरविच्छिन्नैस्तमः सूर्य इवांशुभिः ॥

meaning.en: Then Indra's son, enraged, struck down that great army with unbroken nets of arrows, as the sun destroys darkness with its rays.

verses.text:
ततो भग्ने बले तस्मिन्विप्रयाते समन्ततः ।
सव्यसाचिनि संक्रुद्धे त्रैगर्तान्भयमाविशत् ॥

meaning.en: When that force was broken and scattered on every side, and the left-handed archer was enraged, fear entered the Trigartas.

verses.text:
ते वध्यमानाः पार्थेन शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ।
अमुह्यंस्तत्र तत्रैव त्रस्ता मृगगणा इव ॥

meaning.en: Struck by Partha with bent-jointed arrows, they were confused, here and there, like frightened herds of deer.

verses.text:
ततस्त्रिगर्तराट्क्रुद्धस्तानुवाच महारथान् ।
अलं द्रुतेन वः शूरा न भयं कर्तुमर्हथ ॥

meaning.en: Then the king of the Trigartas, enraged, said to those great chariot-warriors, "Enough of running, heroes; you should not be afraid.

verses.text:
शप्त्वा तु शपथान्घोरान्सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ।
गत्वा दौर्योधनं सैन्यं किं वै वक्ष्यथ मुख्यगाः ॥

meaning.en: Having taken terrible oaths in sight of the whole army, what will you say, you chiefs, when you go back to Duryodhana's army?

verses.text:
नावहास्याः कथं लोके कर्मणानेन संयुगे ।
भवेम सहिताः सर्वे निवर्तध्वं यथाबलम् ॥

meaning.en: Will we not become objects of ridicule in the world for this deed in battle? Turn back together, each as he can."

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते राजन्नुदक्रोशन्मुहुर्मुहुः ।
शङ्खांश्च दध्मिरे वीरा हर्षयन्तः परस्परम् ॥

meaning.en: Thus addressed, O king, they shouted again and again, and the heroes blew conches, cheering each other.

verses.text:
ततस्ते संन्यवर्तन्त संशप्तकगणाः पुनः ।
नारायणाश्च गोपालाः कृत्वा मृत्युं निवर्तनम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the Samshaptaka bands turned back again, and the Narayanas and Gopalas, making death their return.
